tool_args.rationale: The earlier square-root-only fit was refuted on fresh confirmation, while the purchased gradient contrast shows strong sink-gradient inhibition. The two-layer siphon bridge with a signed local square-root branch captures both the saturating input response and gradient dependence. Fit its three parameters numerically to all seven rows, then use the fitted model for fresh confirmation.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Already acquired; the two added gradient-contrast rows distinguish sink inhibition from a gradient-independent branch.
Rows vary gradient and input at one common horizon, and the bridge-siphon static law is the directly supported mechanism; no trajectory evidence identifies the four- or five-parameter ODE.
All observations share H=0.6, with no evidence of long-horizon reversal; a slow-horizon probe is not justified by these data.
It is irrelevant to the observed smooth flux-conserving response and is explicitly unnecessary.
